Architecture Decision Record: ADR-042
Project: Nexus Core Ledger & Payment Gateway Migration | Status: Approved | Author: Elena
Vance (Lead Solutions Architect) | Date: October 14, 2026
1. Context & Problem Statement
The legacy ledger relies on a monolithic DynamoDB NoSQL cluster with custom eventual-
consistency resolution logic. This has caused reconciliation discrepancies exceeding $42,000
during high-throughput flash events. The engineering organization requires a deterministic,
ACID-compliant ledger storage solution capable of supporting 8,500 financial transactions per
second with real-time auditability.
2. Approved Decision & Rationale
We have decided to adopt PostgreSQL 16 with TimescaleDB hypertables for all double-entry
transaction ledgers, replacing the DynamoDB store.
Documented Rationale:
1. Strict ACID Compliance: Immediate row-level locking and strict serializability are mandatory for
cross-border payment settlement.
2. Audit Query Performance: TimescaleDB hypertables provide native chunking by timestamp,
reducing 90-day forensic audit query execution times from 4 minutes to under 650ms.
3. Regulatory Requirements: Compliance standards (FINRA & European Central Bank DORA
directives) require verifiable point-in-time state reconstruction.
Lead Owner: Elena Vance (Lead Solutions Architect)
Target Delivery: Sprint 43 (October 24, 2026)
Status: Approved and Implementation In Progress
3. External Dependencies & Blockers
Critical Dependency: Core Banking Gateway API v3.4 release by 3rd-party vendor (FinVance Inc.).
Dependency Status: UNRESOLVED. Vendor support ticket #FV-9021 remains open without an
SLA commitment or staging endpoint delivery date.
4. Key Management & Security
A decision was recorded to rotate root AWS KMS customer-managed signing keys on a 14-day
cycle. (Note: No rationale or compliance justification was provided for this 14-day frequency;
standard security policy specifies 90-day rotation).
